steps.why: The question asks for names only, but saying first what a silicate is shows that glass and cement belong to the class asked about. Both are built from the same SiO₄⁴⁻ tetrahedron as the natural silicates.
common_mistakes: Naming feldspar, mica or asbestos. Those are silicates, but they are minerals taken from the ground and not man-made.
Naming silica or sand. Silica is SiO₂ itself, which is an oxide and occurs naturally.
steps.memory_tip: Glass and cement are the two silicates made in a furnace.
steps.margin_note: Write both names on one line; the question asks for two, not one.

steps.why: Naming two natural silicates beside the two man-made ones shows that the difference asked about is how they are obtained, not what they are built from. Every one of them is built from the SiO₄⁴⁻ tetrahedron.
common_mistakes: Writing that man-made silicates have a different basic unit. The unit is the same SiO₄⁴⁻ tetrahedron in both.
Giving one name only. The question asks for two man-made silicates.
steps.memory_tip: Mined means natural, made in a furnace means man-made.
steps.margin_note: One closing line separating the mined silicates from the manufactured ones completes the answer.
